decisions.decision: column `color` is an optional, nullable #RRGGBB hex string; DB column nullable with no backfill; update path deliberately out of scope
decisions.rationale: Requiring it breaks every existing client; backfilling invents a product decision nobody made. Set-once gap filed as a todo.

decisions.decision: Publish composed-constraint patterns via a springdoc PropertyCustomizer that is ALSO registered as a GlobalOpenApiCustomizer
decisions.rationale: swagger-core's ModelResolver.resolveProperties calls applyBeanValidatorAnnotations a second time AFTER the PropertyCustomizer returns, resetting minLength to 1. Only the document-level phase is guaranteed to run last.

decisions.decision: Publish the password regex in the public API document
decisions.rationale: Explicit, informed user decision. Do NOT re-litigate. A prose description is published instead of an example, because a password-shaped literal would trip the repo's gitleaks pre-commit scan.

decisions.decision: Fail closed when translating Java regexes to ECMA-262: publish a pattern only where equivalence is proven by a test, otherwise publish none
decisions.rationale: An absent constraint under-documents; a WRONG constraint makes correct clients reject valid data while looking authoritative. Asymmetric harm.

decisions.decision: Enforce null-safety with NullAway + JSpecify rather than a lint rule banning `== null`
decisions.rationale: Established practice, and it reuses the already-wired net.ltgt.errorprone 5.1.0 / error_prone_core 2.50.0 — no new framework. Critically, NullAway USES null checks to narrow @Nullable to @NonNull, so banning `== null` would break the standard tool. Scope: start at AnnotatedPackages = ...kanban_board.service, one line to widen.

decisions.decision: Fold the expression-oriented null refactor into the NullAway task (user: 'yes fold it')

context_notes: Two quick tasks ran back to back. 260904-obv is DONE and in production. 260904-ss1 is functionally complete and green (514 tests) but has 3 execution-confirmed defects found by a three-way AI review, currently being fixed. The defects are: (D1) @Pattern.flags() silently dropped so DOTALL is lost and the published pattern rejects multi-line and NBSP values the server accepts; (D2) the phase-2 reassert uses unconditional setters so it LOOSENS any field-level @Schema, making the 'Never loosen' comment false; (D3) @Size counts UTF-16 units while JSON Schema counts code points, so 17 emoji pass the document and fail the Validator; (D4) an internal gitleaks note leaked into the public API document via Password's @Schema description. Method note that repeatedly mattered this session: verify that a check actually RAN, not just that it printed nothing — a failed grep and a clean grep look identical, and Gradle's UP-TO-DATE test task looks exactly like a passing one.
